title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, and Upgrade/Rollback
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It combines: reference architectures, recommended on-prem packaging patterns, minimum hardware and network requirements, a prescriptive deployment checklist, day-2 operational runbook, and a controlled upgrade & rollback procedure. Intended audience: SREs, deployment engineers, solutions architects, and customer-facing technical owners.

Scope and audience

- Scope: Production deployments where the Redwood Private control plane is either customer-managed (VPC) or fully on-prem (air-gapped). Covers initial deploy, day-2 ops, and version upgrades/rollbacks. Does NOT cover hosted API usage or dedicated cloud-only managed fleets.
- Audience: Eng SRE, Platform, Customer Solutions, Security.

High-level reference architecture

- Control plane modes:
  - Hosted-private (control plane hosted by Redwood; data plane in customer VPC).
  - Customer-managed control plane (full control in customer VPC or on-prem).
- Components:
  1) Management/control plane (API, console, roster service).
  2) Data plane (GPU inference nodes, autoscaler, router, cache).
  3) Observability stack (prometheus + grafana, distributed tracing, audit logs).
  4) Persistence (etcd/postgres for control plane; S3-compatible object store for model artifacts).

Network & security requirements (minimum)

| Component | Ports / Protocols | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane API | 443 (HTTPS) | TLS1.2+, mTLS optional for customer-managed CP |
| gRPC router <-> workers | 50051, 50052 | Internal-only, recommend host firewall rules |
| KV/Cache | 6379 (redis) or unix socket | Harden and enable AUTH for redis |
| etcd | 2379, 2380 | Clustered etcd with TLS |
| Object store (S3 API) | 443 | Signed credentials, IAM roles preferred |
| Monitoring | 9090 (prometheus), 3000 (grafana) | Expose to monitoring VPC/subnet only |

Network best practices

- Use dedicated subnets for control plane, data plane, and monitoring.
- Use security groups / firewall policies to restrict east-west access.
- Enforce flow logs and packet capture retention for at least 7 days for initial deployments.
- For on-prem: run control plane behind an internal load balancer with mTLS to workers.

Hardware and packaging recommendations (on-prem)

- GPU node sizing (typical):
  - Small: 1x A10G or A16 (for pilot / dev)
  - Medium: 4x A100-40GB (for steady production throughput ~200-300 rps of short prompts)
  - Large: 8x A100-80GB or H100 (for high throughput / large-context models)
- CPU: 8 vCPU per GPU minimum for serving containers.
- Memory: 64 GB RAM per GPU machine recommended; for 80GB models increase to 96-128 GB.
- Storage: NVMe local for model shards (1-3 TB), and separate durable object store for artifacts (S3/NAS).
- Packaging options:
  1) Single-rack reference: 4 GPU servers + 2 control plane nodes + 2 monitoring/infra nodes; use redundant top-of-rack switches.
  2) Multi-rack scaling: shard model serving by rack with cross-rack load balancing; use BGP/ECMP for network resilience.

Prerequisites (customer/tactical)

- VPC with at least three subnets (control, workers, monitoring).
- IAM roles or equivalent with permissions for: object store read/write, secrets, and metrics export.
- TLS certificates (CA chain) for control plane and internal mTLS if enabled.
- Access to hardware (if on-prem): IPMI/BMC access recommended for remote management.

Deployment checklist (step-by-step)

1) Validate prerequisites: network, IAM, certificates, storage.
2) Provision infra: control plane nodes, worker nodes, load balancers, and monitoring nodes.
3) Install base OS and security hardening (disable unused services, enable auditd, configure sysctl recommended settings).
4) Bootstrap control plane: etcd cluster, postgres, object-store buckets, and apply TLS certs.
5) Register worker nodes with control plane (agents) and verify health.
6) Upload model artifacts to object store and run model verification (checksum + sample inference).
7) Run canary traffic against a single worker rack, observe latency and error budgets.
8) Scale to target capacity and enable autoscaling policies.
9) Configure observability dashboards and alert rules (see standard alerts below).
10) Execute acceptance tests and handover to customer ops.

Day-2 operational runbook (common tasks)

- Routine checks (daily):
  - Control plane: etcd health, DB replication lag < 5s, API 99.9% success rate last 24h.
  - Data plane: GPU utilization, OOM events, model load failures, sequence length distributions.
  - Monitoring: Prometheus scrape success > 99%; alerting channel active.
- Incident triage quick steps:
  1) If API errors spike: check control plane pods, DB CPU, and etcd.
  2) If latency increases: check worker queue, KV cache hit rate, and batching metrics.
  3) If GPU OOM/model load fail: inspect model shard placement and restart affected worker after core dump upload.
- Escalation matrix:
  - Triage lead (oncall-sre) -> Runtime owner -> Platform engineering -> Solutions eng (customer)

Standard alerts (examples)

- controlplane_api_5xx_rate > 1% over 5m -> Sev2
- etcd_unavailable_nodes > 0 -> Sev1
- gpu_memory_utilization > 92% for 10m -> Sev2
- model_load_fail_rate > 0.5% over 15m -> Sev2

Upgrade and rollback procedure (controlled flow)

Principles: roll upgrades conservatively (canary -> staggered -> full), keep a tested rollback artifact, maintain at least one healthy control plane replica, and validate observability and acceptance tests after each stage.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Backup postgres and etcd (snapshots stored offsite).
- Verify terraform/iac snapshot of current infra.
- Confirm model artifact hashes and compatibility with runtime version.
- Clear pending maintenance windows and notify stakeholders.
- Run smoke test suite and record baseline metrics.

Canary upgrade (recommended):
1) Select single non-critical worker rack and drain traffic.
2) Deploy runtime + kernel updates to canary workers.
3) Run compatibility test: 1000 sample requests (latency, correctness) and gather metrics for 30m.
4) If metrics within SLO and no regressions, proceed to staggered rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%).
5) Monitor for 60-120m between stages and run automated data quality checks (prompt set regressions).

Rollback steps (if canary or staged rollout fails):
1) Halt rollout immediately and move traffic away from failing nodes (use routing policy).
2) Redeploy previous runtime artifact to the affected workers.
3) If control plane is impacted, promote standby replica and restore etcd/postgres snapshot if required.
4) Postmortem and RCA within 72 hours; capture metrics and binary diffs.

Customer requirements library (quick reference)

| Requirement | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Control plane replicas | 3 | 3 | HA; quorum for etcd |
| Worker GPU memory | 40GB | 80GB | Depends on model family; list supported models in onboarding checklist |
| Storage throughput | 500 MB/s | 2 GB/s | For large model streaming |
| Network latency (intra-rack) | < 1ms | < 0.5ms | Affects KV cache and batching effectiveness |
| Audit log retention | 30 days | 365 days | For regulated customers may increase to 7 years |

Packaging and distribution notes (on-prem)

- Use container images signed with cosign; image registry either in-VPC or on-prem artifactory.
- Provide an offline bundle for air-gapped installs: images.tar, manifests.yaml, checksums.sha256, and installation script (install.sh).
- Validate bundle integrity with SHA256 and GPG signature verification as part of install preflight.

Verification & acceptance tests (post deploy)

- Functional: model inference correctness against golden prompt sets (pass rate > 99%).
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency within baseline \u00b115%; throughput meets target TPS.
- Reliability: no new 5xx errors, no OOMs for 2 hours at target load.

Troubleshooting snippets

- Check worker agent logs (example):
  kubectl -n redwood logs deployment/worker-agent --since=1h | grep -i error
- Rebalance model shards:
  redwoodctl model rebalance --model my-model --concurrency 4
- Restore etcd snapshot (control plane):
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /backups/etcd-snap.db --name etcd-restore --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restored
